notes: Derived edit: parent_headquartered_in is the immediate owner (direct_subsidiary_of, functional: 'the company that owns it') composed with headquartered_in, kept as a firm rule (the definitional premise). Two derived-belief worlds: Pixar's owner gives way (w1) or Disney's headquarters does (w2). Since 2026-10-31 the adds hold only the side facts the worlds name, not the answer (FINDINGS E): w1, a new owner headquartered in some city; w2, Disney headquartered in some other city (placeholders). New York City then follows from the edit and the rule, since parent_headquartered_in is functional. 'Burbank is in California' and 'New York City is in the state of New York' are the record's bridges. q1 ('the same US state as Pixar itself') is a join: the parent's headquarters city lies in a state that contains Pixar's headquarters city. Pixar in Emeryville, California is q1's bridge, and 'a city lies in one US state' is firm, stated per named city as a class axiom with a nominal (located_in is transitive, so it can't be functional, and a rule would not fire on the join's unnamed state). Relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check. Since the justification review of 2026-10-31, the US-state typing (state_kinds) is its own item, 'a city lies in one US state' (one_state) is stated for Emeryville and Burbank only, and 'no place is in both New York and California' (states_disjoint, firm, definitional) replaces the per-city axiom for New York City, so q1's 'no' goes through the bridge 'New York City is in the state of New York' (nyc_ny).

background.states_disjoint: located_in value new_york_state ⊑ not (located_in value california)

queries.ask: pixar : parent_headquartered_in some (located_in some (USState and inv(located_in) some (inv(headquartered_in) value pixar)))

fol.notes: One uninterpreted sort. headquartered_in and parent_headquartered_in are functions (RELATIONS.md: functional); the parent rule is the firm definitional premise, as in the DL file. 'Same US state' needs a place to be in one US state (firm) and California and New York to be distinct. Pixar's own headquarters (Emeryville, California) is a firm bridge: it moves in neither world.

pixar_disney.says: Pixar is owned by the Walt Disney Company. (premise)

disney_burbank.says: The Walt Disney Company is headquartered in Burbank. (premise)

parent_rule.says: A company's parent company is the company that owns it: its parent's headquarters city is that owner's.
parent_rule.z3: ForAll([a, p], Implies(direct_subsidiary_of(a, p), parent_headquartered_in(a) == headquartered_in(p)))

nyc_ny.says: New York City is in the state of New York.

pixar_emeryville.says: Pixar is headquartered in Emeryville, California. (stored)

states.says: California and New York are two different US states.

one_state.says: A place is in one US state.
one_state.z3: ForAll([x, s, t], Implies(And(us_state(s), us_state(t), located_in(x, s), located_in(x, t)), s == t))
